 29,000 Baby Brezza Bottle Sterilizers Recalled Due to Burn Hazards
 The Baby Brezza SuperFast Sterilizer Dryer can overheat during use. No injuries have been reported.
 By 
 Jessica D’Argenio Waller, MS, CNS, LDN, CPST 
 Baby & Health Writer 
 November 5, 2026 
 After reports that the Baby Brezza SuperFast Sterilizer Dryer overheats during use, the company is recalling 29,000 units. 
 Source: CPSC
 Baby Brezza has recalled 29,000 units of a baby bottle sterilizer after reports that it can overheat during use and cause a burn hazard. No injuries have resulted from use of the Baby Brezza SuperFast Sterilizer Dryer , but the company has received 32 reports of overheating when the unit is plugged in, including some in which the plastic casing has melted.
 The countertop appliance is used to sterilize and dry baby bottles, breast pump parts, and accessories in 10 minutes. The product was sold from January 2024 to October 2026 for between $160 and $180 at babybrezza.com, babylist.com, and target.com, and at TJ Maxx and Marshalls stores across the country. 
 More on Baby Safety 
 Baby Product Recalls Parents Should Know About 
 Three Baby Formula Makers Didn't Work Effectively in CR's Evaluations 
 CR's Baby Bottle Sterilizer Ratings 
 Owners should stop using the recalled Baby Brezza bottle sterilizer immediately, the Consumer Product Safety Commission says, and dispose of the product properly, as outlined below.
 Baby Brezza is offering consumers a free replacement sterilizer dryer, the Baby Brezza SuperQuick 10 Minute Sterilizer Dryer, which the company says is “an upgraded model” that offers “more features and benefits.” There’s no refund available at this time.  
 4 Best Baby Bottle Sterilizers of 2026, Tested and Reviewed
 CR tested for cleaning effectiveness and ease of use. Here are the four baby bottle sterilizers we recommend . 
 Baby Brezza Sterilizer Recall Details
 Products recalled: 29,000 Baby Brezza SuperFast Sterilizer Dryers have been recalled for overheating when plugged in and in use, posing a risk of injury or burn hazards. 
 Affected model numbers: The recalled sterilizers have model numbers BRZ0083, BRZ0154, and BRZ0156 and were sold in two colors. The model number is printed on a label on the bottom of the unit.
 The problem: The company has received 32 reports of sterilizers overheating or their plastic housings melting. No injuries have been reported.
 What to do next: Stop using the recalled sterilizer immediately, the company says, even if it appears to be working normally. Unplug the unit and store it away from flammable objects. You can contact Baby Brezza for a free replacement after registering your product and uploading a photo on the company site . You do not need a receipt. The CPSC recommends cutting the power cord to destroy the sterilizer dryer before disposing of it in accordance with your local restrictions. 
 Jessica D’Argenio Waller, MS, CNS, LDN, CPST
 Jessica D’Argenio Waller is a baby and health writer and editor at Consumer Reports, covering a range of topics, from strollers to infant formula to safe sleep practices. Before joining CR in 2025, she was editorial director at Motherly. Jessica is a licensed and board-certified nutritionist and a certified child passenger safety technician, a mom of two, and an avid runner and home cook.
